summary: Both round-3 divergences are fixed and structurally sound. (1) AC4/AC8 fallback trace: `fallback_reason` is now attached in BOTH consumers, at the identical point and under the identical guard — shared/scripts/lib/llm_review.py:222-223 and shared/scripts/tools/external_review.py:392-393, `if openai_route_note and "openai" in reviews and openai_route != "none"`, immediately after the `as_completed` loop. The guard is exactly the fallback-happened-and-something-ran case: `resolve_openai_route` (external_review_default_legs.py:275/281) returns a non-empty note ONLY when gpt_leg.provider=='codex' and codex is unavailable, and the `!= "none"` arm hands the same note to the skip branch's `reason` (llm_review.py:214, external_review.py:385), so no path loses it now. docs/guide.md:1514 Option D's 'says so in the recorded reason' is backed on both the succeeded-fallback and skipped-fallback paths. Covered by shared/tests/test_llm_review.py:174 `test_run_review_records_fallback_reason_on_a_successful_fallback_leg`, which also asserts the note is NOT smeared onto the glm leg; the CLI's copy is line-for-line identical, verified by reading it. (2) Scope: the mini-plan (.shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-09-03-codex-cli-review-leg-MINIPLAN.md:97-103) now records `shared/glossary.md` as an attributed extra with its rationale; the glossary edit is confined to the existing 4-line External-Review entry (glossary.md:493-496) and the file ends at line 540, i.e. still at its cap, matching the net-neutral claim. Re-derived the touched-file set by grepping the worktree for every new symbol (`gpt_leg`, `review_codex`, `resolve_openai_route`, `is_codex_available`, `codex_settings`, `api_route`, `fallback_reason`): the hits are exactly the mini-plan's `## Files touched` list plus the run's own planning artifacts. AC1 review_codex (default_legs.py:158) reuses classify_reply + the SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT prose contract, no new schema. AC2 is_codex_available (:120) returns rather than raises on every path including timeout/OSError. AC3 external_review.json gpt_leg.provider default 'api' + gpt_leg_provider() (external_review_config.py:217) over the existing deep-merge. AC5 ('openai','codex') -> ('codex','gpt-5.6-terra') in _REVIEW_MODEL_BINDINGS (external_review_routing.py:55) plus models.codex, with mismatch-rejection tested. AC6 both consumers call the same resolver and dispatch GLM purely off OPENROUTER_API_KEY, independent of openai_route. AC7 holds structurally: for provider=='api' the resolver returns `api_route(...)`, bit-identical to the old detect_provider chain, and the CLI's envelope `provider` is unchanged on that path. AC8 both docs updated (guide.md:1514 Option D, hooks-and-pipeline.md:2950 config data-flow row). Non-Goals all respected: no GLM codex route, no env-var route override (only the pre-existing, identity-backstopped SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_MODEL_CODEX model-name pattern, which the mini-plan's rejected-alternative section explicitly distinguishes), and pr_review_model_policy.py untouched. Stage 2 (code-reviewer) may now run.
